title: 07. Google ADK: Day 1 — ADK Foundations: Install, Architecture & First Agent
summary: Get Google ADK v2.7.0 running, understand the stack, build your first agent in 60 minutes

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
Get Google ADK v2.7.0 running, understand the stack, build your first agent in 60 minutes

Day 1 / 15
ADK v2.7.0 (Aug 2026)
Python 3.10+

🎯 Learning Objectives

- Understand what Google ADK is and how it differs from LangChain / AutoGen

- Install ADK v2.7.0 (August 2026 release) and verify the CLI

- Scaffold a project with `adk create` and understand the file layout

- Build a minimal hello-world agent with one tool and run it via `adk run`

- Compose multi-tool agents and enforce structured Pydantic output

sections.title: 1. Why Google ADK?
sections.body:
**Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)** is Google's first-party framework for building production-grade AI agents. Released as **v2.0 GA on May 19, 2026** and refined through **v2.7.0 (August 13, 2026)**, it is the same framework that powers agents on Google Cloud's Agent Platform.

### How it differs from LangChain / AutoGen / CrewAI

| Dimension | LangChain | AutoGen | CrewAI | **Google ADK** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Origin** | Community | Microsoft research | Community startup | Google first-party |
| **Architecture** | Chain-of-prompts | Conversational roles | Role-based crew | **Graph-based workflow runtime** |
| **Model support** | Many LLMs via wrappers | OpenAI-centric | Many LLMs | Gemini native + LiteLLM (100+ LLMs) |
| **Deployment** | DIY | DIY | DIY | **First-class Cloud Run / Agent Runtime** |
| **State management** | Memory classes | Manual | Manual | **Built-in Session/State/Memory/Artifact services** |
| **Multi-agent** | LCEL chains | Conversational | Crew roles | **Sub-agents + Workflow graph + A2A protocol** |
| **Production-ready** | Medium | Low | Medium | **High (Google SLA)** |

ADK's defining characteristic is that it treats agents, tools, and functions as **nodes in a workflow graph** (since v2.0). This means you get deterministic orchestration, typed data flow, human-in-the-loop pauses, and automatic retries — all built into the framework rather than bolted on.

💡 Key Concept

ADK is **not** a thin wrapper around the Gemini SDK. It is a full **agent runtime** with its own session management, event loop, callback system, and deployment story. Think of it as "what if Next.js + Vercel were purpose-built for AI agents, by Google, for Google Cloud."

The v2.7.0 release (August 2026) is described in Google's release notes as *"a correctness release: most of the work went into what an agent sends to the model and what it gets back."* This means the API surface is stable and production-ready — perfect timing to learn it.

sections.title: 2. The ADK Architecture Stack
sections.body:
Before writing code, internalize this stack. Every ADK concept you'll learn over the next 14 days fits somewhere in this diagram.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        ADK ARCHITECTURE STACK                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│   ┌─────────────┐   ┌─────────────┐   ┌─────────────┐              │
│   │   adk web   │   │   adk run   │   │ adk api_srv │   ← CLI      │
│   └──────┬──────┘   └──────┬──────┘   └──────┬──────┘              │
│          │                 │                 │                     │
│          └────────────┬────┴─────────────────┘                     │
│                       ▼                                             │
│              ┌─────────────────────┐                                │
│              │       Runner        │   ← orchestrates runs          │
│              └──────────┬──────────┘                                │
│                         │                                           │
│        ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐                          │
│        ▼                ▼                ▼                          │
│  ┌───────────┐   ┌────────────┐   ┌────────────┐                   │
│  │  Agent    │   │  Session   │   │  Memory    │                    │
│  │ (LlmAgent)│   │  Service   │   │  Service   │                    │
│  └─────┬─────┘   └─────┬──────┘   └────────────┘                   │
│        │               │                                           │
│        ▼               ▼                                           │
│  ┌───────────┐   ┌────────────┐                                   │
│  │   Tools   │   │   Events   │                                    │
│  │ FuncTool  │   │  Actions   │                                    │
│  │ McpToolset│   │  Deltas    │                                    │
│  └─────┬─────┘   └────────────┘                                   │
│        │                                                           │
│        ▼                                                           │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────┐                                 │
│  │     LLM (Gemini/OpenAI/      │                                 │
│  │     Claude via LiteLLM)      │                                 │
│  └───────────────────────────────┘                                 │
│                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```python
# Display the architecture diagram generated for this course
from IPython.display import Image, display
display(Image(filename="images/day01_architecture.png"))
```

### Layer-by-layer walkthrough

1. **CLI layer** — Three entry points: `adk web` (browser-based dev UI), `adk run` (interactive CLI), `adk api_server` (FastAPI REST server). All three ultimately invoke the Runner.

2. **Runner** — The orchestrator. You give it an agent + session_service, and it manages the full invocation lifecycle: fetch session → run agent → yield events → persist state. The `run_async()` method returns an `AsyncIterator[Event]` you consume with `async for`.

3. **Services** — Four pluggable services:
   - **Agent** (the LlmAgent itself — your prompt + tools)
   - **Session Service** (InMemory / Database / VertexAi — stores conversation state)
   - **Memory Service** (semantic long-term recall across sessions)
   - **Artifact Service** (binary file storage — PDFs, images, JSON blobs)

4. **Tools & Events** — Tools are functions the LLM can call (auto-wrapped from Python functions, or MCP toolsets, or other agents). Events are the unit of communication — every state change, tool call, and LLM response is an `Event` object yielded by the Runner.

5. **LLM Backend** — Gemini is native (just pass a model string). OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and 100+ others work via `LiteLlm(model="openai/gpt-4o")`. ADK abstracts away provider differences.

🚀 Pro Tip

Keep this architecture diagram open in a separate tab while you learn. Every ADK error message, every confusing behavior, every "where does this state live?" question can be answered by tracing through these layers.

diagrams.title: Google ADK architecture stack
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TB
  UI["adk web / adk run / your FastAPI app"] --> RN["Runner - drives one invocation"]
  RN --> AG["Agent tree - LlmAgent, SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent"]
  AG --> TL["Tools - FunctionTool, AgentTool, MCPToolset, google_search"]
  AG --> MD["Model - Gemini or LiteLLM (OpenAI, Anthropic)"]
  RN --> SS[("SessionService - events + state")]
  RN --> MS[("MemoryService - long-term recall")]
  RN --> AS[("ArtifactService - files, blobs")]
diagrams.explain: In ADK you **declare** agents; the **Runner** executes them. For each user message the Runner loads the session from the **SessionService**, runs the agent tree, and records every step as an **Event**. Memory and artifacts are separate services, so you can swap in-memory implementations for databases or Vertex AI without touching agent code.

sections.title: 3. Installation (v2.7.0, August 2026)
sections.body:
### Prerequisites

- **Python 3.10 or later** (check with `python3 --version`)
- `pip` (comes with Python)
- A virtual environment tool (`venv`, `uv`, `conda` — your choice)

### Step 1: Create a virtual environment

```bash
# Using venv (built-in)
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # macOS / Linux
# .venv\Scripts\activate.bat         # Windows CMD
# .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1         # Windows PowerShell
```

### Step 2: Install ADK

```python
# Install the core ADK package (v2.7.0, August 2026)
pip install google-adk==2.7.0

# Optional extras based on your needs:
# !pip install google-adk[gcp]              # Vertex AI / Agent Runtime (Google Cloud)
# !pip install google-adk[db]               # DatabaseSessionService (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite)
# !pip install google-adk[a2a]              # A2A protocol (agent-to-agent)
# !pip install google-adk[bigquery-analytics]  # NEW in v2.7.0 — BigQuery analytics plugin
# !pip install "litellm>=1.84"              # LiteLLM connector (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.)
```

**Output**

```text
Collecting google-adk==2.7.0
  Downloading google_adk-2.7.0-py3-none-any.whl (1.2 MB)
Collecting google-genai>=1.0.0
Collecting pydantic>=2.0
Collecting fastapi>=0.115.0
Successfully installed google-adk-2.7.0 google-genai-1.4.0
```

⚠️ Important

**v2.7.0 breaking change**: `pyarrow` (~50 MB) moved out of the `[gcp]` extra into the new `[bigquery-analytics]` extra. If you previously relied on `BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin` via `google-adk[gcp]`, you must now install `google-adk[bigquery-analytics]` explicitly.

```python
# Verify installation
adk --version
```

**Output**

```text
ADK 2.7.0\n
```

```python
# List all CLI commands
adk --help
```

**Output**

```text
Usage: adk [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...\n\n  Google Agent Development Kit CLI\n\nOptions:\n  --version  Show the version and exit.\n  --help     Show this message and exit.\n\nCommands:\n  api_server     Start FastAPI REST server\n  web            Start FastAPI server with Web UI\n  run            Interactive CLI session\n  create         Scaffold a new agent project\n  deploy         Deploy to Cloud Run / Agent Engine / GKE\n  eval           Run evaluation\n  eval_set       Manage eval sets\n  test           Run pytest on agent test JSON files\n  conformance    Conformance testing\n  migrate        Migrate session DB schema\n  optimize       Agent optimization workflows\n  telemetry      Manage CLI usage telemetry\n
```

sections.title: 4. Project Structure
sections.body:
Use `adk create` to scaffold a project. This generates the canonical layout ADK expects.

```python
# Scaffold a new agent project
adk create my_first_agent
```

**Output**

```text
Sample agent created at my_first_agent/\n\nNext steps:\n  1. cd my_first_agent\n  2. Add your API key to .env\n  3. Run: adk run my_first_agent\n
```

The generated structure:

```text
my_first_agent/
├── agent.py        # main agent code (MUST define `root_agent`)
├── __init__.py     # contains: from . import agent
└── .env            # API keys / project IDs
```

### Critical convention: `root_agent`

ADK looks for a variable named **`root_agent`** in your `agent.py` module. This is the entry point — the agent that `adk run`, `adk web`, and `adk api_server` will execute. If you name it anything else (e.g. `my_agent`, `agent`), ADK won't find it.

💡 Key Concept

The `__init__.py` file must contain `from . import agent` (or whatever your module is named). This makes `root_agent` importable as `my_first_agent.agent.root_agent`, which is what the ADK CLI uses to load your agent.

sections.title: 5. Four Progressive Examples
sections.body:
Now we'll build four agents, each more capable than the last:

1. **Example 1** — Minimal hello-world: one agent + one tool (get_current_time)
2. **Example 2** — Add a second tool (weather) and see auto-delegation
3. **Example 3** — Realistic assistant with 3 tools and proper config
4. **Example 4** — Structured output via Pydantic `output_schema`

Example 1: Hello-World Time Agent

Minimal agent with one tool — the "Hello World" of ADK

This is the absolute minimum viable agent. Note four things:

1. **Import** — `from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent` (the canonical `LlmAgent` alias)
2. **Tool function** — a plain Python function with a docstring (ADK reads the docstring to generate the tool's description for the LLM)
3. **Agent construction** — name, model, description, instruction, tools
4. **`root_agent`** — the magic variable name ADK looks for

```python
# agent.py — Example 1: Hello-World Time Agent
from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent

def get_current_time(city: str) -> dict:
    """Returns the current time in a specified city.

    Args:
        city (str): The name of the city to get the current time for.
    """
    # In production, call a real time API here
    import datetime
    # Mock: pretend we looked up the city's timezone
    now = datetime.datetime.now()
    return {
        "status": "success",
        "city": city,
        "time": now.strftime("%H:%M"),
        "timezone": "UTC",  # would be city-specific
    }

# The magic variable ADK looks for
root_agent = Agent(
    name="time_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",  # or 'gemini-flash-latest'
    description="Tells the current time in a specified city.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a helpful assistant that tells the current time in cities. "
        "Use the 'get_current_time' tool for this purpose. "
        "Always respond in a friendly, concise manner."
    ),
    tools=[get_current_time],
)

print(f"Agent created: {root_agent.name}")
print(f"Model: {root_agent.model}")
print(f"Tools: {[t.name if hasattr(t, 'name') else t.__name__ for t in root_agent.tools]}")
```

**Output**

```text
Agent created: time_agent\nModel: gemini-2.0-flash\nTools: ['get_current_time']\n
```

### Running the agent

Save the code above as `my_first_agent/agent.py`, then run:

```python
# Set your Gemini API key (get one free at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)
import os
os.environ["GOOGLE_API_KEY"] = "YOUR_GEMINI_API_KEY_HERE"

# Run via ADK CLI
adk run my_first_agent
```

**Output**

```text
Welcome to ADK! You are now interacting with time_agent.\n\nType 'exit' to quit.\n\n>>> What time is it in Tokyo?\nCalling tool: get_current_time(city='Tokyo')\nTool result: {'status': 'success', 'city': 'Tokyo', 'time': '14:32', 'timezone': 'UTC'}\n\nIt's currently 14:32 in Tokyo. Note: the time shown is in UTC — in production,\nthis tool would resolve the city's actual timezone (JST, UTC+9) and return 23:32.\n
```

🚀 Pro Tip

**Get a free Gemini API key** at [https://aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). The free tier is generous — 15 requests/minute on `gemini-2.0-flash`, more than enough for learning.

For OpenAI or Anthropic instead of Gemini, see Example 4 below — you just swap the `model=` parameter.

Example 2: Multi-Tool Assistant

Add a second tool and watch the LLM auto-select the right one

Real agents need multiple tools. ADK makes this trivial — just add more functions to the `tools=[...]` list. The LLM reads each function's docstring and signature, then decides which to call based on the user's query.

```python
# agent.py — Example 2: Multi-Tool Assistant
from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent
from google.genai import types

def get_current_time(city: str) -> dict:
    """Returns the current time in a specified city.

    Args:
        city (str): The name of the city.
    """
    import datetime
    return {
        "status": "success",
        "city": city,
        "time": datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M"),
    }

def get_weather(city: str, unit: str = "Celsius") -> dict:
    """Retrieves the weather for a city.

    Args:
        city (str): The city name.
        unit (str): Temperature unit — 'Celsius' or 'Fahrenheit'. Defaults to 'Celsius'.
    """
    # Mock weather data — replace with real API call in production
    mock_data = {
        "Tokyo": {"temp_c": 22, "condition": "Partly Cloudy"},
        "London": {"temp_c": 15, "condition": "Rainy"},
        "New York": {"temp_c": 18, "condition": "Sunny"},
    }
    data = mock_data.get(city, {"temp_c": 20, "condition": "Clear"})
    temp = data["temp_c"]
    if unit == "Fahrenheit":
        temp = temp * 9 / 5 + 32

    return {
        "status": "success",
        "city": city,
        "temperature": temp,
        "unit": unit,
        "condition": data["condition"],
    }

def get_population(country: str) -> dict:
    """Returns the approximate population of a country.

    Args:
        country (str): The country name.
    """
    populations = {
        "Japan": 125800000,
        "UK": 67500000,
        "USA": 331000000,
        "India": 1380000000,
    }
    pop = populations.get(country, "Unknown")
    return {"country": country, "population": pop}

root_agent = Agent(
    name="city_info_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Answers questions about cities: time, weather, and country population.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a helpful city information assistant. You can tell users about:\n"
        "- Current time in a city (use get_current_time)\n"
        "- Weather in a city (use get_weather)\n"
        "- Population of a country (use get_population)\n\n"
        "Always use the appropriate tool. Be concise and friendly."
    ),
    tools=[get_current_time, get_weather, get_population],
    generate_content_config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0.2,          # low temp = more deterministic
        max_output_tokens=250,    # keep responses short
    ),
)

print("Multi-tool agent ready!")
print(f"Available tools: {[t.name if hasattr(t,'name') else t.__name__ for t in root_agent.tools]}")
```

**Output**

```text
Multi-tool agent ready!\nAvailable tools: ['get_current_time', 'get_weather', 'get_population']\n
```

### What happens at runtime

When the user asks *"What's the weather in Tokyo and what time is it there?"*, the LLM:
1. Parses the query into two intents (weather + time)
2. Calls `get_weather(city='Tokyo')` → receives `{temp: 22, condition: 'Partly Cloudy'}`
3. Calls `get_current_time(city='Tokyo')` → receives `{time: '14:32'}`
4. Synthesizes a natural-language response combining both results

All of this happens automatically — you just provide the tools and a good instruction.

```
USER MESSAGE
     │
     ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   Runner    │  ← run_async(user_id, session_id, new_message)
└──────┬──────┘
       │ fetches Session (state + events history)
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   Agent     │  ← _run_async_impl(ctx)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│ before_model_cb │  ← optional guardrail / cache
└────────┬────────┘
         │ None → continue
         ▼
┌─────────────┐
│     LLM     │  ← generate_content_async(contents, config)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│ after_model_cb  │  ← optional response modification
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         ▼
   ╔═══════════════╗
   ║  Tool call?   ║
   ╚══════╤════════╝
      YES │           NO
          ▼            ▼
   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────────┐
   │ run tool │   │ yield Event  │ ← is_final_response() = True
   └────┬─────┘   └──────────────┘
        ▼
   ┌──────────────┐
   │ after_tool_cb│
   └──────┬───────┘
          ▼
   loop back to LLM
```

Example 3: Realistic Travel Assistant

Production-style agent with config tuning and output_key state saving

Now we add three production-grade features:

1. **`generate_content_config`** — control temperature, max tokens, safety settings
2. **`output_key="travel_response"`** — auto-saves the final text to `session.state["travel_response"]` for use by downstream agents
3. **Async tools** — tools can be `async def` for I/O-bound work (HTTP calls, DB queries)

```python
# agent.py — Example 3: Realistic Travel Assistant
import asyncio
import httpx
from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent
from google.genai import types

async def fetch_flight_price(origin: str, destination: str, date: str) -> dict:
    """Fetches the cheapest flight price for a route on a given date.

    Args:
        origin (str): IATA code of origin airport (e.g. 'JFK').
        destination (str): IATA code of destination airport (e.g. 'HND').
        date (str): Travel date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    """
    # Mock: in production, call Skyscanner / Amadeus / Duffel API
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # simulate network latency
    base_prices = {"JFK-HND": 850, "LHR-DXB": 320, "SFO-SIN": 1100}
    key = f"{origin}-{destination}"
    price = base_prices.get(key, 500)
    return {
        "origin": origin,
        "destination": destination,
        "date": date,
        "price_usd": price,
        "currency": "USD",
        "airline": "Mock Airlines",
    }

async def fetch_hotel_price(city: str, checkin: str, checkout: str) -> dict:
    """Fetches the cheapest hotel price for a city and date range.

    Args:
        city (str): City name.
        checkin (str): Check-in date YYYY-MM-DD.
        checkout (str): Check-out date YYYY-MM-DD.
    """
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    nightly = {"Tokyo": 120, "Dubai": 200, "Singapore": 150}
    rate = nightly.get(city, 100)
    return {
        "city": city,
        "checkin": checkin,
        "checkout": checkout,
        "nightly_rate_usd": rate,
        "currency": "USD",
    }

def get_exchange_rate(from_currency: str, to_currency: str) -> dict:
    """Returns the current exchange rate between two currencies.

    Args:
        from_currency (str): Source currency code (e.g. 'USD').
        to_currency (str): Target currency code (e.g. 'JPY').
    """
    rates = {"USD_JPY": 149.5, "USD_EUR": 0.92, "USD_SGD": 1.34}
    key = f"{from_currency}_{to_currency}"
    rate = rates.get(key, 1.0)
    return {"from": from_currency, "to": to_currency, "rate": rate}

root_agent = Agent(
    name="travel_assistant",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Helps users plan trips by fetching flight, hotel, and currency info.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a travel planning assistant. When a user describes a trip:\n"
        "1. Fetch flight prices with fetch_flight_price (convert city names to IATA codes yourself)\n"
        "2. Fetch hotel prices with fetch_hotel_price\n"
        "3. If they mention a foreign currency, get the exchange rate\n"
        "4. Summarize the total estimated cost in USD\n\n"
        "Be proactive — if they say 'Tokyo next month', ask for specific dates.\n"
        "Always show a final cost breakdown."
    ),
    tools=[fetch_flight_price, fetch_hotel_price, get_exchange_rate],
    generate_content_config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0.3,         # slightly creative for natural summaries
        max_output_tokens=500,
        top_p=0.9,
    ),
    output_key="travel_response",  # auto-save final text to session.state
)

print(f"Travel assistant '{root_agent.name}' configured.")
print(f"output_key: {root_agent.output_key}  (final response saved to state)")
print(f"Temperature: {root_agent.generate_content_config.temperature}")
```

**Output**

```text
Travel assistant 'travel_assistant' configured.\noutput_key: travel_response  (final response saved to state)\nTemperature: 0.3\n
```

💡 Key Concept

**`output_key` is huge for multi-agent systems.** When you chain agents (Day 10), the second agent can read `session.state["travel_response"]` in its instruction via `{travel_response}` templating. This is how ADK agents pass data to each other without manual plumbing.

We'll see this in action on Day 11 (SequentialAgent) and Day 12 (Graph Workflow).

Example 4: Structured Output + Multi-LLM (OpenAI / Claude)

Enforce Pydantic schemas and swap LLM providers with LiteLlm

Two advanced features in one example:

1. **`output_schema`** — pass a Pydantic `BaseModel` class and the agent's response is guaranteed to match that schema (returned as JSON)
2. **`LiteLlm`** — swap Gemini for OpenAI GPT-4o or Anthropic Claude with one line

```python
# agent.py — Example 4: Structured Output + Multi-LLM
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent
from google.adk.models.lite_llm import LiteLlm

# Pydantic schema — the agent's final response MUST match this
class TripPlan(BaseModel):
    destination: str = Field(description="City and country, e.g. 'Tokyo, Japan'")
    total_cost_usd: float = Field(description="Estimated total cost in USD")
    flight_cost: float = Field(description="Flight cost in USD")
    hotel_cost: float = Field(description="Hotel cost in USD")
    duration_days: int = Field(description="Trip duration in days", ge=1, le=30)
    summary: str = Field(description="One-paragraph trip summary")
    tips: list[str] = Field(description="3-5 practical travel tips")

# Option A: Gemini (default — just pass model string)
gemini_agent = Agent(
    name="trip_planner_gemini",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Generates a structured trip plan as JSON.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a travel planner. Given a destination and budget, produce a detailed plan.\n"
        "Always respond with the structured TripPlan schema. Be specific with numbers."
    ),
    output_schema=TripPlan,
    # NOTE: output_schema + tools only works together on Gemini 3.0+.
    # For other models, omit tools when using output_schema.
)

# Option B: OpenAI GPT-4o via LiteLLM
openai_agent = Agent(
    name="trip_planner_openai",
    model=LiteLlm(model="openai/gpt-4o"),  # requires OPENAI_API_KEY
    description="Same trip planner, powered by GPT-4o.",
    instruction=gemini_agent.instruction,
    output_schema=TripPlan,
)

# Option C: Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet via LiteLLM
claude_agent = Agent(
    name="trip_planner_claude",
    model=LiteLlm(model="anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"),  # requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    description="Same trip planner, powered by Claude.",
    instruction=gemini_agent.instruction,
    output_schema=TripPlan,
)

# Use whichever you have an API key for:
root_agent = gemini_agent  # swap to openai_agent or claude_agent as desired

print(f"Active agent: {root_agent.name}")
print(f"Model: {root_agent.model}")
print(f"Output schema: {root_agent.output_schema.__name__}")
print(f"Schema fields: {list(root_agent.output_schema.model_fields.keys())}")
```

**Output**

```text
Active agent: trip_planner_gemini\nModel: gemini-2.0-flash\nOutput schema: TripPlan\nSchema fields: ['destination', 'total_cost_usd', 'flight_cost', 'hotel_cost', 'duration_days', 'summary', 'tips']\n
```

⚠️ Important

**`output_schema` + `tools` limitation**: Only **Gemini 3.0+** supports both simultaneously. For OpenAI/Claude, you must choose one or the other — either structured output OR tool calling, not both.

**v2.7.0 fix**: Models now declare their own capabilities, so ADK won't silently fail — it will raise a clear error if you try to combine them on an unsupported model.

**Workaround for non-Gemini**: Use a "formatter sub-agent" pattern — agent A calls tools and produces free-text, agent B (with `output_schema`) formats A's output into JSON. We'll build this on Day 11.

🚀 Pro Tip

**Install LiteLLM once, use 100+ LLMs**: `pip install "litellm>=1.84"`. Then any of these work:
- `LiteLlm(model="openai/gpt-4o")`
- `LiteLlm(model="anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022")`
- `LiteLlm(model="ollama/llama3")` (local)
- `LiteLlm(model="mistral/mistral-large-latest")`
- `LiteLlm(model="deepseek/deepseek-chat")`

Set the corresponding env var (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, etc.) and you're done.

sections.title: Day 1 Summary
sections.body:
📌 Key Takeaways

- **ADK v2.7.0 (August 2026) is a stable, production-ready framework — install with `pip install google-adk==2.7.0`**

- **Every agent project needs a `root_agent` variable in `agent.py` — that's the entry point ADK looks for**

- **Tools are just Python functions with docstrings — ADK auto-wraps them. No decorators, no boilerplate**

- **`generate_content_config` controls temperature, max tokens, top_p — tune per use case (low temp for math, higher for creative)**

- **`output_schema` (Pydantic) enforces structured JSON output — but only Gemini 3.0+ supports it alongside tools**

- **Swap LLMs with `LiteLlm(model='openai/gpt-4o')` — same agent code, different provider**

- **Use `output_key='key_name'` to auto-save agent responses to session state for downstream agents to read**
